name: breast overview
title: A breast complaint divided by how she presents: a lump (benign or worrisome, imaged by age then sampled), breast pain (cyclical or mastitis), nipple discharge (galactorrhea or pathological, usually a papilloma) and screening (usual or high risk, with carcinoma in situ split into DCIS and LCIS); each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and management, with the biopsy risk tiers and genetic testing below

root.title: A breast problem: how is she PRESENTING?
lines: most breast lumps are NOT cancer · the OLDER she is, the more likely any complaint is serious
every one: history (age, cycle, family history) · offer a chaperone · examine both breasts + every node group

groups.title: A LUMP: benign or WORRISOME on exam?

pres.title: When you investigate
lines: • IMAGE BY AGE: < 35 ULTRASOUND (breast too dense, risk too low for a mammogram; MRI if high risk), > 35 MAMMOGRAM ± ultrasound
• then SAMPLE: fine needle aspiration → core biopsy → excision

pres.title: Exam: a mass or suspicious finding?

head: h
Benign lump
fibroglandular tissue · cyst · FIBROADENOMA · fibrocystic change
clue: • fibrocystic: lumpy, changes with her CYCLE
inv: 1 · Pre-menopausal: recheck after her NEXT PERIOD
2 · Not resolved → image by age, sample
tx: Benign biopsy: the report sets her risk

head: h
Fat necrosis
BENIGN, but closely MIMICS cancer
inv: it feels like cancer: only the biopsy tells them apart

head: h
Invasive carcinoma
malignant cells invade the stroma
clue: • skin change, peau d'orange, nipple retraction: LATE
inv: also if post-menopausal or high risk
tx: • estrogen / progesterone receptor (ER/PR) POSITIVE → tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor
Axillary NODES: the key prognostic factor

head: h
Cyclical pain
hormonal: ducts (estrogen), stroma (progesterone)
tx: birth control pill or hormone replacement therapy (HRT)

head: h
Mastitis
also non-cyclical: medicines, Cooper's ligament stretch, extramammary
inv: 2 · Not lactating or persistent: rule out CANCER
tx: • lactating: KEEP breastfeeding, empty the breast
• not lactating: imaging OK → repeat in 3 months

head: h
Galactorrhea
physiological: not pregnancy or lactation
not from a breast lesion
clue: • clear, yellow, grey, brown or green

head: h
Pathological: PAPILLOMA
the commonest · also duct ectasia, fibrocystic change, CANCER
inv: galactogram maps the duct, but is NOT diagnostic
tx: the only way to be sure

head: h
Carcinoma IN SITU
ductal (DCIS) or lobular (LCIS)
intact myoepithelial layer: NOT invaded
clue: on a biopsy for something else

panels.title: The benign biopsy report sets her cancer risk
items: proliferative without atypia, ×1.5–2: papilloma, sclerosing adenosis, radial scar
ATYPICAL hyperplasia, ×4–5 (×9–10 with a family history) → screen YEARLY

panels.title: Screening + genes
items: HIGH risk, YEARLY mammogram: 1st-degree relative < 50, or two at any age · ovarian cancer · male breast cancer in the family · atypia, LCIS, radial scar, phyllodes · density > 75%
usual risk: NOT ultrasound, MRI, clinical breast exam or self-exam
GENETIC TESTING if she has breast cancer and is < 35 · < 50 with two affected relatives · male · Ashkenazi Jewish
BRCA carrier: yearly MRI + mammogram · prophylactic mastectomy ± oophorectomy · tamoxifen
